claims.text: Adding Cr, V, or Hf to existing high-entropy alloys can improve their mechanical properties.
Adding Cr, V, or Hf to existing high-entropy alloys can improve their thermal stability.
Adding Cr, V, or Hf to existing high-entropy alloys can improve their resistance to radiation damage.
Compositionally optimized high-entropy alloys are suitable for lightweight applications.
Compositionally optimized high-entropy alloys provide superior comprehensive performance.
Adding alloying elements can alter chemical short-range order in high-entropy alloys.
Adding alloying elements can alter the grain size of high-entropy alloys.
Adding alloying elements can alter the precipitation of secondary phases in high-entropy alloys.
Changes in chemical short-range order, grain size, and secondary-phase precipitation lead to improved mechanical properties.
Changes in chemical short-range order, grain size, and secondary-phase precipitation lead to improved thermal stability.
Changes in chemical short-range order, grain size, and secondary-phase precipitation lead to improved resistance to radiation damage.
High-entropy alloys have limitations in ductility, toughness, and scalability.
The exact effects of specific alloying-element additions on high-entropy-alloy properties remain uncertain.
